settings.solHelp.title: How to configure Sleep-on-LAN
settings.solHelp.intro: The 💤 button in NetDash sends a SOL magic packet to the host. For sleep to work, each target machine must run an agent listening on a UDP port (default 9).
settings.solHelp.gptwolHint: Alternatively, set a GPTWOL URL above — NetDash will send WoL/SOL via the gateway instead of locally.
settings.solHelp.linuxDesc: Install sleep-on-lan (pip or Docker). The agent listens on UDP and sleeps when it receives a packet with the reversed MAC.
settings.solHelp.linuxFirewall: Firewall: allow UDP port 9 (or another sol_port from NetDash settings).
settings.solHelp.windowsDesc: Use the sleep-on-lan Windows port, Depicus WakeOnLan tools, a custom PowerShell UDP listener, or another SOL agent. Run as a service (NSSM or Task Scheduler at startup).
settings.solHelp.windowsFirewall: Windows Firewall: inbound UDP rule for the chosen port (default 9).
settings.solHelp.macosDesc: Install sleep-on-lan or a custom UDP script. pmset handles local sleep, but SOL requires a persistent network listener on the host.
settings.solHelp.macosFirewall: System Settings → Network → Firewall: allow the SOL agent application.
modal.solHelpLink: How to enable SOL on the host?
settings.sol.scripts.title: SOL host install scripts
settings.sol.scripts.hint: Run the selected script on the target machine (as root / administrator). It listens on the SOL UDP port from NetDash settings and suspends the host when a reversed-MAC magic packet is received.
settings.sol.scripts.serviceHint: Script tailored to this service's MAC. Run it on the target host.
settings.sol.scripts.security: Requires administrator privileges. Firewall must allow UDP from the NetDash server subnet. Enable Wake-on-LAN in BIOS (for the ⚡ button).
